segments.t: Trying to cure his nightmares, Denis lies in bed repeating Vika's advice to think about something pleasant—and ends up dreaming about Vika herself. When the real Vika asks him the next day to help move a couch in her office, just like in his dream, Denis panics. Let's listen to the scene in Russian.
Нужно чаще думать о чём-то приятном.
И тогда все плохие сны пройдут.
Привет, Денис, поможешь мне в кабинете?
Мне там надо диван немного отодвинуть.
Да, конечно, я сейчас тебе помогу.
Ну, скажи, как твои ночные кошмары?
Всё хорошо, я сделал как ты сказала.
Я думал о приятном перед сном.
Спасибо тебе большое за твою помощь.
Не надо благодарить меня за это.
Я рада, что помогла тебе.
Мне вчера собака ногу сильно укусила!
Now let's trace the way Denis's dream collides with reality line by line.
Нужно чаще думать о чём-то приятном.
'I need to think about something pleasant more often.' Lying in bed, Denis repeats Vika's exact words using an indefinite pronoun in the prepositional case.
И тогда все плохие сны пройдут.
'And then all the bad dreams will pass.' He hopes that positive thoughts will banish his recurring nightmares.
Привет, Денис, поможешь мне в кабинете?
'Hi, Denis, will you help me in the office?' In Denis's dream—and later in reality—Vika asks for help using a perfective future verb.
Мне там надо диван немного отодвинуть.
'I need to move the couch a little in there.' The prefixed perfective infinitive means to push or move something aside.
Да, конечно, я сейчас тебе помогу.
'Yes, of course, I will help you right now.' Denis agrees to help using a dative personal pronoun and a perfective future verb.
Ну, скажи, как твои ночные кошмары?
'Well, tell me, how are your nightmares?' Back in the real restaurant, Vika checks on Denis using a nominative plural noun phrase.
Всё хорошо, я сделал как ты сказала.
'Everything is fine, I did as you said.' Denis reports his success using a masculine past verb and a feminine past verb.
Я думал о приятном перед сном.
'I thought about something pleasant before sleep.' The preposition meaning before governs the instrumental singular of the noun meaning sleep.
Спасибо тебе большое за твою помощь.
'Thank you very much for your help.' The preposition meaning for takes the feminine accusative singular noun meaning help.
Не надо благодарить меня за это.
'There is no need to thank me for that.' A negated modal predicate pairs with an imperfective infinitive and accusative pronoun.
Я рада, что помогла тебе.
'I am glad that I helped you.' A feminine short predicate adjective introduces a clause with a dative personal pronoun.
Мне вчера собака ногу сильно укусила!

'A dog bit my leg badly yesterday!' Realizing Vika just repeated her lines from his erotic dream, Denis blurts out an excuse and limps away. Let's hear the scene with Denis and Vika again from start to finish.

Terrified that his dream about Vika is coming true, Denis invents a ridiculous story about a giant dog biting his leg. Listen for the nouns meaning couch, nightmares, and help. See you in the next scene.
